questions.question: Which state is geographically NOT a contiguous part of the North-East region?
questions.explanation: Sikkim is geographically not a contiguous part of the North-East region and is separated by the Siligudi corridor.

questions.question: What is the common description for the seven contiguous states of North-East India?
questions.explanation: The contiguous seven states are commonly described as the 'Land of Seven Sisters'.

questions.question: Sikkim plays the role of being a ________ to the 'Seven Sisters'.
questions.explanation: Sikkim has taken up the role of being a little brother to the amazing seven sisters.

questions.question: Most of the festivals celebrated in the North-East are based on which activity?
questions.explanation: Many of the festivals in North-East India are based on agriculture.

questions.question: Which major cultural festivals are celebrated in a series of three in Assam?
questions.explanation: Bihus are among the major cultural festivals of Assam and consist of a series of three prominent festivals.

questions.question: Rongali Bihu is also known by which other name?
questions.explanation: Rongali Bihu is also known as Bohag Bihu.

questions.question: When is Rongali Bihu celebrated?
questions.explanation: Rongali Bihu is celebrated in mid-April.

questions.question: Which Bihu marks the start of the New Year in Assam?
questions.explanation: Rongali Bihu marks the start of a New Year in Assam.

questions.question: Kongali Bihu is celebrated when the fields are lush but the ________ are empty.
questions.explanation: Kongali Bihu is celebrated in mid-October when the fields are lush but the barns are empty.

questions.question: What is the alternative name for Kongali Bihu?
questions.explanation: Kongali Bihu is also called Kaati Bihu.

questions.question: What do people do during Kongali Bihu to guide souls to heaven?
questions.explanation: On Kongali Bihu, people light lamps and pray to God to guide souls to heaven.

questions.question: Which Bihu is a thanksgiving festival observed in mid-January?
questions.explanation: Bhogali Bihu, also called Magh Bihu, is observed in mid-January as a thanksgiving.

questions.question: Bhogali Bihu symbolises the end of the ________.
questions.explanation: The Bhogali Bihu festival symbolises the end of the harvest season.

questions.question: The Bihu dance is characterized by which movements?
questions.explanation: The Bihu dance is performed with brisk steps and hand movement.

questions.question: What is the 'pepa' in Assamese culture?

options.B: A wind instrument made of buffalo horn

questions.explanation: The pepa is a wind instrument made of buffalo horn used in Bihu celebrations.

questions.question: Which instrument is described as being similar to a drum in Bihu?
questions.explanation: The dhol is similar to a drum and used during the Bihu dance.

questions.question: Arunachal Pradesh is known for its lush green paddy fields and _________ mountains.
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh features lush green paddy fields and pine clad mountains.

questions.question: Which is the most important New Year festival in certain areas of Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The new-year festival, Losar, is the most important festival in certain areas of Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.question: Mopin is the harvest festival of which tribe?
questions.explanation: Mopin is the harvest festival of the Galo tribe in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.question: Which goddess is worshipped during the Mopin festival?
questions.explanation: During Mopin, people worship goddess Mopin to drive away evil spirits.

questions.question: What is 'Popir'?
questions.explanation: Popir is an indigenous folk dance performed by young women during Mopin.

questions.question: In which month is the Ziro Festival of Music held?
questions.explanation: The Ziro festival of music is held at Ziro in September every year.

questions.question: The Ziro Festival features how many indie bands from across the world?
questions.explanation: The music congregation features a combination of 30 indie bands and top folk acts.

questions.question: Which Manipuri festival revives relationships between married girls and their parents?
questions.explanation: Ningol Chakouba binds and revives the relationships between married girls and their parents.

questions.question: What do villagers in Manipur do as part of the Cheiraoba ritual?
questions.explanation: As part of Cheiraoba, villagers climb the nearest hilltops to help them rise to a higher plane in life.

questions.question: Cheiraoba is the New Year festival of which state?
questions.explanation: Cheiraoba is the Manipur new-year festival celebrated in April.

questions.question: What is Chapchar Kut commonly known as in Mizoram?
questions.explanation: The Spring Festival or Chapchar Kut is an important occasion in Mizoram.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT mentioned as adding to the festive air of Chapchar Kut?
questions.explanation: Drums, gongs, and cymbals are mentioned for Chapchar Kut; the pepa is Assamese.

questions.question: The Wangala festival is also known as the ___________ festival.
questions.explanation: Wangala is also known as the Hundred-drum Festival.

questions.question: Which tribe in Meghalaya celebrates the Wangala festival?
questions.explanation: Wangala is the most important festival celebrated by the Garos in Meghalaya.

questions.question: In which month is the Wangala harvest festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: The Wangala harvest festival is celebrated in November.

questions.question: The Wangala dance features two parallel lines of which people?
questions.explanation: The dance has two parallel lines – one of men and the other of women.

questions.question: How many gods are worshipped during Karachi Puja of Tripura?
questions.explanation: Karachi Puja is marked by worshipping fourteen gods.

questions.question: Where does Karachi Puja take place?
questions.explanation: The festival takes place in old Agartala or Puran Heveli.

questions.question: Karachi Puja is celebrated as per the instructions of which deity?
questions.explanation: They worship fourteen gods as instructed by Lord Shiva.

questions.question: Dances in Tripura often represent activities like hunting and ________.
questions.explanation: Many dances in Tripura represent hunting, food-gathering, and other activities.

questions.question: Songs and dances in Nagaland festivals help in preserving what?
questions.explanation: Celebration of these festivals is an effective means of preserving and passing down their oral history.

questions.question: Which Naga festival is celebrated mainly after the sowing season?
questions.explanation: A major Naga festival is Moastu, celebrated mainly after the sowing season.

questions.question: Naga headgear is often decorated with feathers and __________.
questions.explanation: Headgear is decorated with feathers and wild boar tusks.

questions.question: Which state's most admired bird is the Hornbill?
questions.explanation: The Hornbill is Nagaland's most admired bird.

questions.question: How long is the Hornbill Festival?
questions.explanation: The Hornbill festival is a 10-day long event.

questions.question: The Hornbill festival showcases the cultural heritage of how many tribes?
questions.explanation: The event showcases the cultural heritage of 16 tribes.

questions.question: What do men show off during the Hornbill festival dance?
questions.explanation: Men in warrior costume show off their hunting and warring skills.

questions.question: Sikkim festivals are celebrated as per which calendar?
questions.explanation: Sikkim festivals are celebrated as per the Buddhist calendar.

questions.question: Saga Dawa commemorates which three events of Lord Buddha's life?
questions.explanation: Saga Dawa commemorates the birth, enlightenment and death of Lord Buddha.

questions.question: When is Saga Dawa celebrated?
questions.explanation: Saga Dawa is celebrated on the full moon day in the Tibetan lunar month between May and June.

questions.question: In which festival do people visit monasteries and offer butter lamps?
questions.explanation: During Saga Dawa, people visit monasteries and offer prayers, incense sticks and butter lamps.

questions.question: Which Sikkim festival is celebrated at the end of the harvest season with the Chaam dance?
questions.explanation: Losoong is celebrated at the end of the harvest season with the Chaam dance.

questions.question: What do locals wear while performing the Chaam dance?
questions.explanation: Locals wearing brightly coloured masks perform the Chaam dance.

questions.question: Which contest is held during the Losoong festival celebrations?
questions.explanation: An archery contest is held during the Losoong celebrations.

questions.question: Losar is the Tibetan ________ festival.
questions.explanation: Tibetan New Year, Losar, is marked with immense joy.

questions.question: Which Sikkim festival is similar to Diwali?
questions.explanation: Tihaar is the festival of light, somewhat like Diwali.

questions.question: The festivals help bring out the natural ________ of the people.
questions.explanation: Celebrations help bring out the natural talent of the people.

questions.question: What does the word 'contiguous' mean?
questions.explanation: Glossary: contiguous - touching, sharing the boundaries with others.

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'brisk' in the context of Bihu dance?
questions.explanation: Glossary: brisk - quick and energetic.

questions.question: What does 'picturesque' mean?

options.B: Very attractive or charming to look at

questions.explanation: Glossary: picturesque - a place very attractive or charming to look at.

questions.question: The term 'sumptuous' used for Manipuri feasts means:

options.B: Very rich and with a lot of variety

questions.explanation: Glossary: sumptuous - very rich and with a lot of variety.

questions.question: What is 'oral history'?

options.B: Historical information not written but passed on by people

questions.explanation: Glossary: oral history - collection of historical information not written but passed on by people.

questions.question: Which of these is a percussion instrument made with bamboo boards?
questions.explanation: Glossary: bamboo clapper - a percussion instrument made with boards of bamboo.

questions.question: Assam is blessed with the mighty River ________.
questions.explanation: Blessed with lush greenery and the mighty River Brahmaputra.

questions.question: People pray during Bihu for a ________ harvest season.
questions.explanation: People pray to God for a thriving harvest season.

questions.question: Arunachal Pradesh lies farther ________ in the mountain region of the Himalayas.
questions.explanation: Lying farther north in the mountain region of the Himalayas.

questions.question: What do people do with 'the old' during Losar?
questions.explanation: People clean their homes and discard the old to bring in the New Year.

questions.question: Which of these states is NOT among the 'Land of Seven Sisters'?
questions.explanation: Sikkim is not included in the 'Land of Seven Sisters'.

questions.question: In Wangala, men ________ while the lines move forward.
questions.explanation: While the men beat the drums, the lines move forward together.

questions.question: Karachi Puja takes place in which month?
questions.explanation: The festival takes place in the month of July.

questions.question: A temple in Tripura houses how many deities?
questions.explanation: There is a temple that houses 14 deities.

questions.question: Songs and dances form the ________ of Nagaland festivals.
questions.explanation: Songs and Dances form the soul of these festivals.

questions.question: The Hornbill festival is held in which month?
questions.explanation: The event is held in December every year.

questions.question: Which animal's sacrifice is mentioned in Karachi Puja?
questions.explanation: Karachi Puja is marked by animal sacrifice.

questions.question: Which state has 'picture-perfect paddy fields' according to the text?
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh is one of India's most remote locations with lush green paddy fields.

questions.question: In 'Land of Seven Sisters', there is ________ on each other.
questions.explanation: They are described as 'Land of Seven Sisters' because of their interdependence.

questions.question: The Bihu songs have been handed down through many ________.
questions.explanation: The songs have been handed down through many generations.

questions.question: Which term means 'wonderful' or 'very surprising'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: amazing - wonderful.

questions.question: Which term means 'religious rites'?
questions.explanation: Glossary: ritual - religious rites.

questions.question: The word 'commemorate' means:

options.B: To remind people of an important person or event

questions.explanation: Glossary: commemorate - to remind people of an important person or event from the past.

questions.question: Which Sikkim festival usually takes place in February?
questions.explanation: Losar is usually held in February.

questions.question: Festivals in the seven states offer thanks to gods for harvest or ________.
questions.explanation: People offer thanks to the gods for a good harvest or prosperity.

questions.question: Festivals also help ask for protection against ________.
questions.explanation: People offer thanks... or ask for protection against calamities.

questions.question: North-East India is a place of ________ cultures.
questions.explanation: The north-eastern regions of India is a place of diverse cultures.
